operations.title: Add seats to a subscription
notes: Accepted at any point in the term and prorated - unlike a decrease, there is no window.
quantity is the new TOTAL seat count, not a delta.
Rejected while the subscription is suspended (2001).

operations.title: Remove seats from a subscription

guard.condition: must still be in the future; read it off the live subscription before attempting the change

notes: The single most common lifecycle mistake: seat reduction is bounded by the same deadline as cancellation, while seat increase is not.
Past the deadline, schedule the smaller seat count for the next term with create-scheduled-changes.
Not supported at all while suspended - the subscription's refundableQuantity comes back null in that state.

operations.title: Move to a different offer (NCE transition)

guard.condition: the target must appear in get-subscription-transition-eligibilities; use the catalogItemId it returns as toCatalogItemId

notes: New Commerce path. Legacy subscriptions use the /upgrades route instead - see get-subscription-upgrades.
eligibilityType=immediate transitions now; eligibilityType=scheduled targets the next term.
transitionType decides whether assigned user licenses move with the subscription.
Poll get-subscription-transitions afterwards - a transition is asynchronous.

operations.title: Cancel a subscription

guard.condition: must still be in the future; the refund on offer is described by refundOptions

notes: A full-resource PATCH with status "deleted" - there is no DELETE verb for a subscription.
Past the deadline the only lever left is turning autorenew off, which lets the subscription expire at term end while still billing the current term.
Software subscriptions and perpetual software cancel at the ORDER instead - see cancel-software-purchase.
Suspending is NOT cancelling: it stops service without stopping billing.

operations.title: Change what the subscription renews into

guard.condition: must be true, otherwise the scheduled instructions are never applied

notes: Term duration, billing cycle and seat count cannot change mid-term; this is how they change at the next term.
Send scheduledActions OR scheduledNextTermInstructions, never both - if both are present only scheduledActions is honoured.
For an immediate move to a different offer use the upgrade operation instead.
For legacy subscriptions the billing cycle changes on the ORDER (update-order), not here (2054).

operations.title: Suspend a subscription
notes: Stops service for the customer but does NOT stop billing - only cancelling inside the cancellation window does that.
Seat count cannot be changed while suspended.
Reversible with the reactivate operation.

operations.title: Reactivate a suspended subscription

guard.condition: must not contain a Microsoft-set reason; a subscription suspended by Microsoft stays suspended until that reason clears

notes: Only valid from suspended. A cancelled (deleted) subscription cannot be reactivated - it has to be repurchased.
Reactivation restores service; the subscription was billed throughout the suspension.

operations.title: Migrate a legacy subscription to New Commerce

guard.condition: validate-migration must return isEligible true for this subscription

notes: Base subscriptions migrate together with all active add-ons as a bundle; if any add-on is ineligible the whole bundle fails.
Asynchronous: poll get-migration, and use get-migration-events for the step-by-step trail.
To run it later rather than now use create-migration-schedule, which can also trigger at the legacy term's renewal.

operations.title: Move billing ownership to another partner

guard.condition: the customer must already have a reseller relationship with the target partner

notes: Created by the TARGET (new) partner; the source partner then accepts (accept-transfer) or rejects (reject-transfer).
The creating partner can back out with update-transfer status "Cancel" or withdraw-transfer while it is still pending.
New Commerce uses transferType 3; legacy subscriptions go through create-legacy-transfer.
A pending transfer blocks other lifecycle writes on the affected subscriptions - check list-customer-transfers when a write is rejected for no obvious reason.
